examDifficulty.heading: Is the CRM Analytics Einstein Discovery Consultant Exam Hard?
examDifficulty.summary: The CRM Analytics Einstein Discovery Consultant exam is moderately difficult. It rewards practical Salesforce experience because many questions ask you to choose the best configuration, design, or troubleshooting approach rather than recall isolated definitions.
bullets: ~65% passing score — build a margin above the minimum before booking.
Scenario-based choices — expect questions that test when to use CRM Analytics, Einstein Discovery, or Dashboards.
Hands-on context matters — candidates who have configured or supported CRM Analytics and Einstein Discovery in a real org are better prepared than candidates who only memorize notes.
examDifficulty.passRateGuidance: Aim for 75%+ on timed practice sets before booking. If your score is below that, review the highest-weight topics first and retake questions until you can explain why each wrong option is wrong.

examFormat.heading: CRM Analytics Einstein Discovery Consultant Exam Format Explained
examFormat.intro: The CRM Analytics Einstein Discovery Consultant exam is a timed Salesforce credential exam. Use the format below to plan pacing and practice-test strategy.
examFormat.scenarioPercent: A meaningful share of questions are scenario-based. The common pattern is a business requirement followed by several plausible Salesforce options; your job is to identify the safest, most maintainable choice for CRM Analytics and Einstein Discovery.
bestWayToPass: Start with the official outline: Map each exam objective to your notes, Trailhead practice, and weak areas before taking full mocks.
Prioritize high-impact topics: Spend extra time on CRM Analytics, Einstein Discovery, and Dashboards because these usually drive the hardest scenario questions.
Practice under time pressure: Use timed question sets so you learn when to move on and return to marked questions later.
Review explanations deeply: Do not just memorize the right option; write down why the other options are less appropriate for the scenario.

certificationCard.description: This exam covers building dashboards, dataflows, and predictive models in CRM Analytics and Einstein Discovery. You’ll need hands-on knowledge of SAQL, dataset security, and deploying AI-driven predictions back to Salesforce records.

keyConcepts.h2: CRM Analytics & Einstein Discovery: Key Concepts for the Exam

blocks.heading: Data Architecture: Datasets & Dataflows
blocks.body: [CRM Analytics](/certifications/crm-analytics-einstein-discovery-consultant) (formerly Tableau CRM / **Einstein Analytics**) stores data in Datasets — optimized columnar data stores separate from the Salesforce database. Dataflows define how data is extracted from Salesforce objects, joined, aggregated, and loaded into datasets — using a JSON-based recipe. Recipes (Data Prep) provide a visual ETL interface for data transformation. External data can be loaded via CSV upload or connected datasets. Incremental sync keeps datasets fresh with only changed records. The consultant exam tests how to design a dataflow for a multi-object scenario (e.g., joining Accounts, Opportunities, and Cases), how to configure incremental sync, and how to troubleshoot failed dataflow jobs.

blocks.heading: Lenses, Dashboards & Stories
blocks.body: Lenses are explorations of a single dataset — ad-hoc visual analysis. Dashboards assemble multiple charts, tables, and filters into a unified analytical experience. Dashboard JSON defines the full layout and query logic — consultants must be able to read and modify dashboard JSON for advanced customization. SAQL (Salesforce Analytics Query Language) powers advanced queries that the UI cannot express. Binding formulas connect filters and widgets — selection in one widget filters another. Stories are AI-generated narratives that explain key drivers in a dataset. The exam tests how to build a dashboard, use bindings for interactive filtering, and write basic SAQL for a custom query.

blocks.heading: Einstein Discovery Insights & Models
blocks.body: Einstein Discovery uses statistical machine learning to find patterns in historical data and generate predictive insights. Stories analyze a dataset and identify the top factors that influence a chosen outcome metric. Predictions deploy a Story as a scoring model — each Salesforce record gets a predicted score. Writeback deploys predictions back to Salesforce fields (e.g., Opportunity Win Probability). Improvement Suggestions recommend actions that increase the probability of a positive outcome. Model refresh keeps predictions current as new data accumulates. The consultant exam tests how to create a Story for a business scenario, interpret the top predictors, and configure writeback to update opportunity or case fields.

blocks.heading: Security: Row-Level & Field-Level Access
blocks.body: [CRM Analytics](/certifications/crm-analytics-einstein-discovery-consultant) uses a separate security model from Salesforce record sharing. Dataset Security Predicates filter rows based on the logged-in user — referencing user fields like role, profile, or a custom attribute. Inheritance mode automatically applies Salesforce **sharing rules** to the dataset. User Attributes defined in CRM Analytics can be used in predicates and SAQL. **Field-level security** hides specific columns from certain users or groups. App sharing (Viewer, Editor, Manager) controls who can access and modify dashboards. The exam tests how to design a security predicate for a hierarchical visibility scenario (managers see their team's data, reps see only their own).

blocks.heading: Deployment, Administration & Integration
blocks.body: [CRM Analytics](/certifications/crm-analytics-einstein-discovery-consultant) apps are deployed using packages (change sets or CLI). Template Apps provide pre-built analytics solutions for Sales, Service, and specific industries. Custom apps extend or replace template apps. Connected objects define the Salesforce data sources for a template app — configuring which objects and fields feed each dataset. Scheduled dataflow runs keep datasets refreshed (up to 24 scheduled runs per day). Admin setup includes enabling CRM Analytics, assigning **permission sets**, and configuring connected objects. Integration with Einstein Discovery requires a CRM Analytics Plus license. The exam tests deployment sequences, template app configuration, and troubleshooting scheduling and data refresh issues.

scenarioTips.h2: How to Pass the CRM Analytics and Einstein Discovery Consultant Exam
scenarioTips.intro: The CRM Analytics exam tests end-to-end analytics implementation: data preparation, story building, dashboard design, and deployment. Focus on the SAQL query language, recipe transformations, and how to embed analytics in Salesforce.

blocks.heading: Dataflow vs. Recipe Architecture
blocks.body: Dataflows use nodes (digest, augment, flatten, edgemart) for batch data preparation. Recipes use visual, step-by-step transformations with live preview. Know when to use each and how they interact.

blocks.heading: SAQL Query Language
blocks.body: SAQL is used in Dashboard JSON and lens queries. Know the key clauses: foreach, group, order, limit, filter, and how to write basic aggregation queries. SAQL knowledge is directly tested.

blocks.heading: Einstein Discovery Stories
blocks.body: Know how to build a Story (outcome field, included variables, excluded variables), interpret Story insights (top factors, improvements), and deploy predictions as Prediction Fields back to Salesforce records.

blocks.heading: Dashboard Design & Embedding
blocks.body: Understand how to configure widgets (chart, number, table, filter), link steps for drill-through navigation, and embed [CRM Analytics](/certifications/crm-analytics-einstein-discovery-consultant) dashboards in Lightning pages and the mobile app.

blocks.heading: Security & Data Access
blocks.body: Know how to configure row-level security using security predicates, user attributes, and dataset sharing inheritance. Understand how Analytics shares (App sharing) control dashboard access.

sampleQuestions.question: What is CRM Analytics (formerly Tableau CRM) used for?
options: Embedded analytics, dashboards, and data exploration on Salesforce data
sampleQuestions.explanation: CRM Analytics provides embedded analytics, dashboards, and data exploration on Salesforce and connected data.
whyWrong: 'Only reports' undersells CRM Analytics' capability — it covers full embedded analytics, not just static reports.
Email is a Marketing Cloud function, unrelated to CRM Analytics' data exploration purpose.
CPQ is a pricing/quoting product, entirely unrelated to CRM Analytics.

sampleQuestions.question: What does Einstein Discovery provide?
options: Predictive insights and recommendations powered by AI
sampleQuestions.explanation: Einstein Discovery delivers AI-powered predictive insights and recommendations.
whyWrong: 'Only charts' undersells Einstein Discovery — it produces AI-driven predictive insights, not just visualizations.
Slack is a collaboration tool, unrelated to Einstein Discovery's predictive analytics function.
Static reports don't involve AI-driven prediction — that contradicts the core function of Einstein Discovery.

sampleQuestions.question: Which role does a CRM Analytics and Einstein Discovery Consultant typically fulfill?
options: Designing and implementing on CRM Analytics and Einstein Discovery in a customer-facing or internal architect role
sampleQuestions.explanation: They design and implement CRM Analytics and Einstein Discovery in customer-facing or architect roles.
whyWrong: Email marketing is a Marketing Cloud function, unrelated to this analytics-focused consulting role.
Slack configuration is a separate specialization, unrelated to CRM Analytics implementation.
UI design alone undersells the role, which spans data architecture, dashboards, and predictive modeling, not just visual design.

sampleQuestions.question: What is a Lens in CRM Analytics?
options: A reusable dataset or query that powers dashboards
sampleQuestions.explanation: A Lens defines a dataset or query that can be reused across dashboards and apps.
whyWrong: A report type is a different Salesforce reporting concept, not a CRM Analytics-specific term.
A Lens isn't an email — it's an interactive data exploration view.
A Lens isn't a campaign — that's a Sales/Marketing Cloud concept unrelated to CRM Analytics.

sampleQuestions.question: Which capability allows users to ask questions in natural language in CRM Analytics?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Einstein Ask allows users to query data using natural language.
whyWrong: 'Only SAQL' undersells the capability — Einstein Ask specifically allows natural language, not just query language.
Dataflow is the ETL pipeline, unrelated to natural language querying.
Dashboard is the visualization layer, not the natural-language query capability being described.

sampleQuestions.question: What is a Dataflow in CRM Analytics?
options: The ETL pipeline that ingests, transforms, and loads data into datasets
sampleQuestions.explanation: Dataflows define the ETL process for building datasets in CRM Analytics.
whyWrong: A report type is a different Salesforce concept, not what a Dataflow does.
A Dataflow isn't an email — it's a data pipeline process.
A Dataflow isn't a dashboard — dashboards are the visualization layer built on top of the data a Dataflow prepares.

sampleQuestions.question: Which language is used to query data in CRM Analytics?
sampleQuestions.explanation: SAQL is used for querying and transforming data in CRM Analytics.
whyWrong: SOQL is the Salesforce Core query language, not what's used for CRM Analytics datasets.
Apex is a programming language, not a data query language used in CRM Analytics.
AMPscript is a Marketing Cloud personalization language, unrelated to CRM Analytics querying.

sampleQuestions.question: What does Einstein Discovery Story provide?
options: Narrative insights and recommended actions based on predictive analysis
sampleQuestions.explanation: Stories deliver narrative insights and recommended actions from predictions.
whyWrong: Static reports don't involve narrative or predictive recommendations — that contradicts what a Story provides.
Dataflows are the ETL pipeline, unrelated to narrative insight generation.
Lenses are exploration views, not narrative predictive stories — that's the specific role of Einstein Discovery Story.

sampleQuestions.question: Which CRM Analytics component displays data in rows and columns?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Tables and grouped tables display tabular data on dashboards.
whyWrong: 'Chart only' undersells the component — it specifically displays tabular row/column data, not charts.
Lens is a broader exploration concept, not the specific grid-display component being asked about.
Dataflow is the data pipeline, unrelated to how data is visually displayed.

sampleQuestions.question: What is the purpose of bindings in CRM Analytics dashboards?
options: To pass filter values between widgets and control interactions
sampleQuestions.explanation: Bindings link widgets so filters and selections flow between components.
whyWrong: Bindings have nothing to do with sending emails — that's a separate function entirely.
Bindings don't run dataflows — that's a separate ETL process.
Bindings don't create lenses — they connect existing widgets/filters together for interaction.

sampleQuestions.question: Which CRM Analytics object stores data for dashboard consumption?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Datasets store the data that lenses and dashboards query.
whyWrong: Lens is an exploration view built on top of a dataset — it isn't itself the storage object.
Report is a different Salesforce Core reporting concept, not the CRM Analytics-specific storage object.
Dataflow is the pipeline that produces data — the actual storage object for dashboard consumption is the dataset.

sampleQuestions.question: What does Einstein Discovery predict?
options: Outcomes (e.g., churn, conversion) and recommends actions
sampleQuestions.explanation: Einstein Discovery predicts outcomes and recommends actions to improve them.
whyWrong: 'Only charts' undersells Einstein Discovery's predictive capability — it forecasts real-world outcomes, not just visuals.
'Only data structure' misrepresents its function — Einstein Discovery predicts outcomes, not schema design.
'Only SAQL' is a query language, unrelated to what Einstein Discovery actually predicts.

sampleQuestions.question: Which governance consideration applies to CRM Analytics?
options: Row-level security, dataset permissions, and data refresh policies
sampleQuestions.explanation: Governance includes RLS, permissions, and refresh policies.
whyWrong: 'None' is incorrect — CRM Analytics has real governance considerations around security and permissions.
'Only email' misrepresents governance scope — it's much broader than email settings.
'Only dashboards' undersells governance, which spans security, permissions, and refresh policies, not just dashboards.

sampleQuestions.question: What is a CRM Analytics App?
options: A container that organizes dashboards, lenses, and datasets for a use case
sampleQuestions.explanation: Apps organize dashboards, lenses, and datasets for specific use cases.
whyWrong: A mobile app is a different concept — a CRM Analytics App is the organizational container within the platform, not a mobile application.
A dataflow alone is just the data pipeline — an App is the broader container that includes dashboards and lenses too.
A lens alone is one exploration view — an App organizes multiple lenses, dashboards, and datasets together.

sampleQuestions.question: Which integration allows CRM Analytics to use Salesforce data?
sampleQuestions.explanation: The Salesforce connector and Data Sync enable CRM Analytics to consume Salesforce data.
whyWrong: Manual export doesn't reflect the native, automated Salesforce integration CRM Analytics actually uses.
Email is unrelated to how CRM Analytics ingests Salesforce data.
Slack is unrelated to CRM Analytics' data integration with Salesforce.
